planting.note: Divide and repot rhizome clumps in spring into a chunky, humidity-retentive mix and keep in warm, bright shade while new roots establish.

directions: This Marantaceae species carries broad, rounded, glossy mid-green leaves on a compact clumping rhizome, distinguishing it from the lance-shaped or elliptic leaves of most other commonly grown calatheas. Grow it out of direct sun in warm, humid, draft-free conditions, since cool drafts and dry air quickly cause the leaf edges to crisp. Keep the mix consistently moist but never soggy, and water with rainwater or distilled water where tap water is heavily fluoridated or softened. Like other calatheas, the leaves rise and fold slightly at night and relax again by day, a trait that gives the family its common prayer-plant nickname.
sources: Kew Plants of the World Online

planting.note: Divide established clumps in spring, pot into a well-drained, organically rich mix, and keep warm and shaded until new growth resumes.

directions: A larger-growing calathea with broad, ribbed, deep-green leaves marked by fine feathered pale-green banding along the lateral veins, giving the foliage a pleated, almost quilted texture. Provide bright but indirect light, since direct sun bleaches the leaf pattern, and maintain high humidity to prevent browning leaf margins. Water thoroughly whenever the top inch of mix dries slightly, and avoid letting the pot sit in standing water. Its larger stature and more upright habit than most calatheas make it a good structural foliage accent toward the back of a shaded houseplant grouping.
sources: Kew Plants of the World Online

planting.note: Divide rhizome offsets in spring and pot into a loose, peat-free humidity-retentive mix, keeping newly divided plants shaded and warm until re-established.

directions: A distinct species from the more commonly sold Maranta leuconeura, this low clumping prayer plant has soft, grayish-green leaves marked with rows of dark brown-green blotches and a quilted texture. Grow it in warm, humid, indirect light, since harsh sun scorches the thin leaves while deep shade causes the markings to fade. Water when the surface of the mix just starts to dry, and reduce watering slightly in winter when growth slows. Like its relatives, the leaves fold upward in the evening and flatten again in daylight, a rhythmic nyctinastic movement that makes prayer plants popular novelty houseplants.
sources: Kew Plants of the World Online

planting.note: Divide trailing stems with roots attached in spring or early summer and pot shallowly into a light, humidity-retentive mix kept warm and shaded.

directions: Unlike the upright-clumping Maranta species usually grown as houseplants, this one has a low, creeping, almost mat-forming habit with small rounded leaves, making it well suited to terrariums, hanging containers, or as a groundcover beneath taller shade plants. Keep it warm and consistently humid, and protect it from direct sun which quickly scorches the thin foliage. Water to keep the shallow root zone evenly moist, since its trailing stems and small leaf surface dry out faster than bulkier Maranta species. Pinch back leggy stems occasionally to keep the planting dense and encourage fresh new growth from the base.
sources: Kew Plants of the World Online
